_doc: Generated by auditing the already-built site (this repo predates the harness workflow — there was no brief to ingest). Each entry: { id, status, builders, nota }.
_status: pending | in_progress | done — only ONE feature may be in_progress at a time.
_builders: subset of [front-end-astro, seo-guide-lines]. Sections -> front-end-astro; close each page with seo-guide-lines.

features.source: .claude/skills/seo-guide-lines/SKILL.md optimization checklist ("Unique meta title, 50-60 characters") + seo-guide-line.md Meta Title section — `generatePageSEO()` at src/config/seo.ts:292 unconditionally appends ` | ${COMPANY_INFO.name}` even when the caller's `title` already ends with a brand fragment, producing duplicated-brand titles outside the 50-60 char range on src/pages/nosotros.astro:25 (77 chars), politicadeprivacidad.astro:12, terminosycondiciones.astro:11, and 404.astro:9.
acceptance: generatePageSEO() strips any trailing brand fragment from options.title (or callers stop including the brand) before appending COMPANY_INFO.name, so the brand appears exactly once in the final title.
Rendered <title> on /nosotros, /politicadeprivacidad, /terminosycondiciones, and /404 each contain the brand name exactly once and fall within (or close to) 50-60 characters.
pnpm build passes; no other page's title regresses (spot-check homepage and one service page title unchanged).
features.nota: Surfaced by the seo-guide-lines compliance review, 2026-09-15.

features.source: .claude/skills/seo-guide-lines/seo-guide-line.md URL Structure section ("canonical must match the exact URL shown in the browser") — src/pages/politicadeprivacidad.astro:6-9,15 sets canonical/breadcrumb path to the non-existent `/politica-de-privacidad` while the real route is `/politicadeprivacidad` (confirmed via Footer.astro:208); src/pages/terminosycondiciones.astro:6-7,14 has the same mismatch (`/terminos-y-condiciones` vs real route `/terminosycondiciones`). acceptance: generatePageSEO({ path: ... }) on both legal pages uses the real route (/politicadeprivacidad, /terminosycondiciones) matching the actual file/URL.
Both pages' breadcrumb schema items use absolute URLs built from COMPANY_INFO.url, consistent with contacto.astro and nosotros.astro.
pnpm build passes; view-source canonical link on both pages matches the URL the page is actually served at.
features.nota: Surfaced by the seo-guide-lines compliance review, 2026-09-15.

features.source: .claude/skills/seo-guide-lines/seo-guide-line.md Content Freshness section (freshness signals must be real, not fabricated) — src/pages/politicadeprivacidad.astro:32 and src/pages/terminosycondiciones.astro:31 render `Última actualización: {new Date().toLocaleDateString()}`, which always shows today's build date rather than the actual last-edit date of the legal text, silently "refreshing" on every rebuild.
acceptance: Both legal pages render a static last-updated date sourced from the actual last content edit (e.g. a frontmatter/const date updated only when the legal text itself changes), not `new Date()` evaluated at build/render time.
The displayed date does not change on a rebuild unless the legal text itself was edited in that same change.
pnpm build passes.
features.nota: Surfaced by the seo-guide-lines compliance review, 2026-09-15. Use git history (`git log --follow -- <file>`) to pick the true last-edit date for the initial value.

features.source: docs/Auditoria_SEO_AEO_ShineAgencia.md:188 ("H1 duplicado en 3 de 4 posts del blog … al escribir, el primer encabezado del cuerpo debe ser '##', nunca '#'"), corroborated at :85-:87 — src/pages/blog/[slug].astro:76 already renders post.data.title as the page <h1>, and the bodies of src/content/blog/ventajas-astro-framework-2026.md:13, seguridad-web-astro-framework.md:20 and marca-personal-ai.md:13 each open with a second '# ' heading, so those 3 posts emit two <h1> elements. marketing-digital-para-abogados.md is already correct (body starts at '##') and must not be touched.
acceptance: The leading '# ' body heading in each of the 3 affected posts is demoted to '## '; the heading text itself is unchanged.
Built HTML for all 4 posts under dist/blog/*/index.html contains exactly one <h1> each.
No heading-level skip is introduced (H1 → H2 → H3, never skipped) in any of the 3 edited posts.

features.nota: Surfaced 2026-09-16 while verifying docs/fix-title-tag-astro-blog.md, which turned out to be a false positive — <title>/og:title are correct in production and in dist/, because PostLayout.astro:22 already feeds post.data.title into generatePageSEO. Side effect of this fix: marca-personal-ai's body is all H3, so the demoted heading becomes its only H2 parent, which also resolves the audit's separate 'salto de jerarquía H1 → H3, sin H2' finding at :190 for that post. Also note the Índice in blog/[slug].astro renders only depth === 2, so each demoted heading will now appear as the first TOC entry on its post — intentional.

features.source: `pnpm check` output on branch feature/04-trailing-slash-and-legacy-redirects, 2026-09-16: 2 errors, both `ts(18048): 'project.data.stack' is possibly 'undefined'` at src/components/section/landing/LatestProjectsAlt.astro:57 and :108. Root cause is in-repo and determinate: src/content.config.ts:18 declares the works collection's `stack` as `z.array(z.string()).optional()`, so `project.data.stack` is typed `string[] | undefined`, while both call sites invoke `.map()` on it without a guard. Not a regression — the component, src/content.config.ts and src/content/works/* are byte-identical to dev. `pnpm build` passes because Astro does not type-check at build time; only `astro check` does, so dev has been red on `pnpm check` independently of any recent work.
acceptance: Both call sites in LatestProjectsAlt.astro (:57, :108) guard the optional array — `project.data.stack?.map(...)` or `(project.data.stack ?? []).map(...)` — rather than making `stack` required in content.config.ts (that is a content-schema change with a wider blast radius, and would need all 10 works entries audited first).
`pnpm check` reports 0 errors across the repo.
`pnpm build` still passes and the two LatestProjects variants render identically for works entries that DO define `stack` (spot-check the homepage).
A works entry with no `stack` field renders the surrounding card without throwing, instead of crashing the map.
features.nota: Surfaced 2026-09-16 during spec 04 step 7. Fixing it was deliberately declined on that branch to keep it scoped to trailing slashes and redirects — see the amended acceptance criterion 5 in specs/04-trailing-slash-and-legacy-redirects.md, which records `pnpm check` as blocked by this pre-existing defect rather than passing.

features.source: Contenido proporcionado por el usuario sobre la evolución de WordPress, webs estáticas, Astro, seguridad, mantenimiento, rendimiento y el papel de la IA.
acceptance: Se crea una entrada Markdown válida en src/content/blog/ con frontmatter compatible con la colección blog.
El artículo compara únicamente Astro y WordPress cuando contrasta una web estática moderna con un CMS tradicional; no presenta Next.js como alternativa.
El artículo explica rendimiento, mantenimiento, seguridad, gestión de cambios y los escenarios en los que WordPress sigue siendo adecuado, con un tono claro y prudente.
El artículo tiene un solo H1 generado por la plantilla, encabezados H2 como preguntas y una llamada a la acción hacia /contacto/.
features.nota: Nuevo artículo SEO/AEO sobre cuándo conviene migrar de WordPress a Astro, con las cifras contextualizadas y sin afirmar que Astro sea invulnerable.

features.source: In-repo duplication, verified 2026-10-13 on feature/16-blog-internal-linking. The same focus-ring class list, `focus-visible:rounded-sm focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-deepplum dark:focus-visible:outline-accentGold`, is written out three times. It is inline in src/components/ui/Breadcrumbs.astro:27. It is copied into a local `linkFocus` const in src/components/section/RelatedPosts.astro:18 and again in src/pages/blog/[slug].astro:47 (both added by spec 16, which reused the Breadcrumbs convention). A change to the site's focus ring would have to be made in three places by hand.
acceptance: The focus-ring class list is defined in exactly one place. Breadcrumbs.astro, RelatedPosts.astro and blog/[slug].astro all consume it, so `grep -rn "focus-visible:outline-deepplum" src` matches only that definition.

The rendered focus behavior is unchanged: in dist/, the links in the breadcrumbs, the RelatedPosts cards and the post's 'Servicio relacionado' aside still get the same outline, offset, rounding and light/dark colors when focused (keyboard spot-check on one post page in light and dark).
No arbitrary `[...]` value or hardcoded color is introduced; only global.css tokens.
pnpm build passes; pnpm check reports no new errors.
features.nota: Requested by the repo owner on 2026-10-13 during spec 16 step 7, as a refactor kept out of spec 16's scope. Moved here from the spec-16 branch so the two branches don't both append to this file. Blocked until spec 16 is merged into dev, because two of the three copies only exist on that branch. Not decided: how the class list is shared, either a Tailwind v4 `@utility` in global.css or an exported TS constant. If it is meant to become the site-wide focus-ring convention for every interactive element (not just these three files), that is a decision no document makes, so route it to /spec instead.
